[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling in Database Design"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Entity-Relationship (ER) modeling is a foundational step in database design. It provides a visual and logical blueprint of how data is structured, related, and constrained within an information system. Mastering ER modeling ensures scalable, maintainable, and highly efficient relational databases."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Components of ER Models"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Entities: Real-world objects or concepts that have an independent existence and can be tracked, such as Customers, Products, or Orders."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Attributes: Specific characteristics or properties of an entity, such as customer_id, first_name, and email."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Relationships: The logical associations or interactions between multiple entities, such as a Customer placing an Order."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Cardinality and Modality"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cardinality defines the numerical mapping between related entities. The primary types are One-to-One (1:1), One-to-Many (1:N), and Many-to-Many (M:N). Modality defines whether the relationship is optional or mandatory."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Translating ER Diagrams to SQL DDL"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the conceptual ER model is finalized, it must be translated into a physical schema using Structured Query Language (SQL). Below is a practical example implementing a One-to-Many relationship between Customers and Orders."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    customer_id INT NOT NULL,
    order_date DATE NOT NULL,
    total_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(customer_id)
    ON DELETE CASCADE
);"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Effective ER Modeling"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use clear, singular nouns for entity names (e.g., 'Customer' instead of 'Customers')."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always define a clear primary key for every entity to ensure row-level uniqueness."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Resolve Many-to-Many relationships using a junction (or associative) table containing foreign keys from both participating entities."}]
